label: SYNTHETIC_UPPER_BOUND
why_this_exists: H2 scored R^2 0.217 against six DSP scalars but only 0.058 against an 80-bin log-spectrogram. A richer baseline scoring WORSE is the signature of either a broken feature pipeline or a genuine generalisation failure. This diagnostic separates the two, because if it were the former the H2 PASS would be manufactured.
finding: The pipeline is not broken. host_spectrogram80 FITS register about as well as the 6 DSP scalars in sample (0.283 vs 0.270) and then fails to generalise to held-out tracks (0.058 vs 0.217). The spectral-shape -> register mapping is arrangement- and instrument-specific; six coarse scalars carry a more transferable version of it. Both baselines leave ~72% of register variance unexplained even in sample.

track_statistics.note: register varies substantially WITHIN tracks, so the target is not a per-track constant the split could leak

LIMITATION_that_qualifies_both_verdicts.statement: Every comparator in J3A is a LINEAR ridge. H1 INCONCLUSIVE and H2 PASS therefore mean 'not LINEARLY recoverable from these baselines', not 'new information'.
LIMITATION_that_qualifies_both_verdicts.consequence: A cheap NONLINEAR read of the frontend already in the product (small MLP or gradient-boosted trees on the same 6 DSP scalars, or on host_spectrogram80) could close the gap. If it does, register is a FEATURE-EXTRACTION change on the M85, not a capability, and no student is warranted.
LIMITATION_that_qualifies_both_verdicts.required_before_any_promotion: run the nonlinear baseline first. This is the DETERMINISTIC_REGISTER_NEXT branch of the pre-registered outcome table, and it is cheaper than any real-audio leg.

does_not_change: the pre-registered thresholds or the v2 verdict. This qualifies how the verdict may be read.
